 HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE PRANAV TRIVEDI  ==================================================

sentences.text: 1 2. The facts in nutshell are that the Food Inspector had collected the sample of 'Tabacco' named Manekchand Gutka (Gutka) from the shop of the accused and after following proper procedure laid down under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/714/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/03/2025 undefined to as the "Act") was sent for analysis and the same came as adulterated.

Thereafter a complaint was filed by the Food Inspector,
Surat Circle before the learned Magistrate, wherein the respondents - accused preferred discharge application before the learned Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Vyara, Tapi being Criminal Case No. 286 of 2002 below Exhibit-96 and Exhibit- 100 inter alia stating that the 'Tabacco' (Gutka) will not come under the provisions of the Act and the Rules and therefore, they may be discharged from the charges.

entities.text: Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Vyara, Tapi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The learned Judge, after considering the issue, discharged the accused persons from the offences levelled against them.
3. Being aggrieved by the order impugned, the present revision application is preferred by the State - applicant.

4. Today, Mr. Hardik Soni, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the State - applicant has raised a specific plea that analysis was carried out and the result was positive wherein the element of 'Magnesium Carbonate' in the sample was more than 0.8%.
Therefore, there was a clear violation of Section 2(ia) (a) (b) read with Section 7(i) of the Act.

It was further submitted that the respondents accused have been discharged on the basis that no standard has been prescribed under the Act and the Rules qua NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/714/2017 JUDGMENT DATED:
27/03/2025 undefined 'Gutka' and therefore, there is no adulteration as per Section 2(i-a)
(a) and (m) of the Act.

4.1. It has further been submitted by Mr. Soni learned Additional Public Prosecutor that as per the requirement of Rule 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 restrictions have been put to use of anticaking agents.
For 'Gutka" no standards are prescribed under the Act and Rules.
Rule 62 is not applicable only to those articles which are prescribed in Act or Rules, but for every food articles in general.
Looking to the requirement of Rule 62 of the Rules, there is a presence of 'Magnesium Carbonate'.
In view of the same, there is breach of Rule 62.
Therefore, the impugned order passed by the learned Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Valsad, Tapi is required to be quashed and set aside.

5. Per contra, Mr. D.K. Modi, learned advocate appearing for the respondent - accused has submitted that the 'Gutka' will not be falling under Schedule-B of the Act and, therefore, there cannot be any allegation of contaminant and adulterated as per the provisions of the Act.

He has strongly placed reliance on the decision of this Court rendered in Criminal Revision Application No.
508 of 2004 dated 08.10.2010.

sentences.text: Heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties and perused the material on record.

The only issue which requires consideration would be whether Rule 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules would come to the aid of the applicant - State to implicate the respondents accused under the provisions of the Act,

However, in one similar set of circumstance where Magnesium Carbonate was found in 'Gutka' and this Court vide order dated 08.10.2010 has observed that provisions of Rule 62 would not be applicable to 'Gutka'.
The relevant observations made in paragraphs 2 to 4 are reproduced hereunder :-

"2. Ms. C.M.Shah, learned APP submits that as per the requirement of Rule 62 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short, "Rules, 1955"), restrictions have been put on use of anticaking agents.

Even, as per report of the Public Analyst,
rule 7(3) of the Rules, 1955 where the test for magnesium carbonate was carried out and the result of the analysis shown `positive'.

Since the opinion given by the Public Analyst that the substance viz. Gutka was misbranded and the sample had not mentioned the list of ingredients declared on the label and, therefore, also provisions of Rule 62 of Rules were violated .
3. Learned APP further submits that considering the above, it is submitted that order of discharge deserves to be quashed and set aside.

4. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perusing the record of the case,
including the impugned order.

Even, the learned APP is unable to dispute that gutka is not mentioned, defined or included under the Act and nowhere standards /
parameters were prescribed in Appendix-B appended to the Act.
In addition to the above, nowhere in the report of Public Analyst it is mentioned that there was breach of any of the standards prescribed under the Act or Rules.

Thus, the decision taken by the learned JMFC in exercise of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.RA/714/2017 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/03/2025 undefined power under section 245(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 based on the decisions of various High Courts,
cannot be said to be in any manner contrary to law, which requires any interference by this Court in revisional powers."
7.

In view of the aforesaid observations and in view of the decisions, this Court see no infirmity in the order passed by the learned Principal Civil Judge and Judicial Magistrate First Class, Vyara,
Tapi.

entities.text:
Judicial Magistrate First Class, Vyara,
Tapi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The case relied on by the respondent is squarely applicable to facts of present case.
Even in matter being Criminal Revision Application No. 508 of 2004, the product was 'Gutka' and Magnesium Carbonate was found.
Even in that case specific plea of Rule 62 was taken and it was rejected.
The order passed in Criminal Revision Application No. 508 of 2004 is not assailed any further.
Therefore, the issue in present case is squarely covered by the decision rendered by this Court in Criminal Revision Application No. 508 of 2004.
In view of the same, the present application being devoid of merits, the same is hereby dismissed.
Rule is discharged.

(PRANAV TRIVEDI,J) phalguni State Of Gujarat Through Divyangkumar ... vs Raghunath Singh Shambhusingh Rajput on 27 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58766651/
